newsitem.title: BRAZIL: SOCCER-CHILAVERT ELECTS HIMSELF WORLD'S BEST GOALKEEPER.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-CHILAVERT ELECTS HIMSELF WORLD'S BEST GOALKEEPER.

text.p: Paraguay's outspoken international Jose Luis Chilavert has elected himself as the world's top goalkeeper.

Chilavert, as famous for his often vicious verbal outbursts as he is for his saves and his rare ability to score goals from free kicks, said in the June issue of the Brazilian magazine Placar that he was also one of the top keepers of all time.

"In 1995, I was elected the best goalkeeper in the world by journalists from Germany and England. For three years in a row, I have won the prize of best goalkeeper offered by the South American Confederation. Yes, I am the best."

Asked where he would figure in an all-time ranking, he said: "I would be in the top three. The other two would be the Italian Dino Zoff, who turned difficult balls into easy balls, and Germany's Harold Schumacher, for his aggressiveness and personality."
Chilavert, who plays for Argentina's Velez Sarsfield, saved some of his harshest words for the Brazilian players who have formed a group called Athletes of Christ.
"I believe in God but you do not have to belong to a group to pray. The Athletes of Christ are the worst, the most violent," he said.
He accused Colombia's Faustino Asprilla of spitting at him during a World Cup game in which both were sent off for fighting. Asprilla was later banned for two games and Chilavert four.
"He spat at me, we pushed each other and were sent off. In the tunnel, when nobody was looking, I punched him in the head."
